analysis.title: ASML: MATCH Act ≠ blanket China DUV ban
key_insights: UBS says concerns that the MATCH Act would impose a blanket ban on DUV shipments to China are overstated, based on its reading of the legislation.

The bill text creates a process to identify 'key chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing equipment' and 'key semiconductor manufacturing facilities' that warrant controls. It also calls for the US to work with allies to align export controls on equipment and components.

Certain advanced immersion DUV systems are already under Dutch export restrictions. MATCH does not say all immersion DUV, or all DUV, is prohibited from sale to China. It appears designed to close gaps between US and allied regimes and possibly extend restrictions around identified equipment and facilities.
The original MATCH Act text names some Chinese companies as entities that 'warrant comprehensive export controls'.
UBS estimates China at about 20%/15%/10% of ASML revenue in 2026/27/28E before any new restrictions, with about 50% of China revenue from immersion.

China was 20% of ASML sales in 9M26, against 26%/28%/32%/32% for Applied Materials/KLA/Lam Research/Tokyo Electron. UBS says ASML's China exposure is now below its US and Japanese peers and close to pre-restriction 2019 levels.

In a stress test where China immersion shipments are largely restricted and affected tools are not reallocated, UBS estimates maximum EPS downside of about 5-10% in 2027E/2028E. The impact could be lower if ASML redirects capacity to other customers.
UBS keeps a Buy rating and a EUR 2,400 12-month price target. The stock closed at EUR 1,236.8 on 17 Nov 2026, implying forecast price appreciation of 94.0%.
UBS EPS estimates are above consensus: EUR 42.22 vs 41.54 for 2026E, EUR 63.42 vs 57.38 for 2027E, and EUR 93.45 vs 75.23 for 2028E.

In the Quantitative Research Review, UBS scores the regulatory/government environment at 2 (getting tougher) and the next EPS update vs consensus at 2 (negative surprise). It also flags a positive catalyst within three months, with no date or description given.

market_movers.rationale: UBS reiterates Buy after judging MATCH Act fears overstated. It puts the maximum EPS hit from a severe China immersion restriction at 5-10% for 2027E/2028E.

sector_views.rationale: UBS says ASML's China exposure of 20% of 9M26 sales is below Applied Materials, KLA, Lam Research and Tokyo Electron (26%-32%). It does not state a sector stance.

earnings_insights: UBS estimates China at about 20%/15%/10% of ASML revenue in 2026/27/28E, with about 50% of China revenue from immersion. These are UBS estimates before any incremental restrictions.
UBS EPS estimates (diluted): EUR 42.22 for 2026E, EUR 63.42 for 2027E, EUR 93.45 for 2028E. Consensus is EUR 41.54, EUR 57.38 and EUR 75.23 for the same years.
The stress-test case, with China immersion shipments largely restricted and no reallocation of tools, gives a maximum EPS downside of about 5-10% in 2027E/2028E.
UBS revenue estimates are EUR 44,447m for 2026E, EUR 60,867m for 2027E and EUR 81,742m for 2028E. EBIT (UBS) is EUR 18,803m, EUR 28,620m and EUR 41,885m.
risk_factors: A broader or accelerated MATCH Act could extend restrictions on identified equipment and facilities in China.
A severe China immersion restriction with no reallocation of tools would cut EPS by about 5-10% in 2027E/2028E, per UBS.
Semiconductor end-market slowdowns could curtail customer capex and defer orders (UBS risk statement).
Cyclicality of customers' businesses and execution risk around next-generation EUV technology (UBS risk statement).
geopolitical: MATCH Act: a US bill that sets a process to identify key chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing equipment and key facilities warranting export controls, and calls for allied alignment of controls.
Dutch export restrictions already cover certain advanced immersion DUV systems.
The original MATCH Act text names some Chinese companies as warranting comprehensive export controls.
UBS refers to a possible acceleration of the MATCH Act 'given the current geopolitical environment'.

tension_points.bull_case: The MATCH Act text sets a process to identify chokepoint equipment and facilities and to align controls with allies. It does not impose a blanket DUV ban, and ASML's China exposure (20% of 9M26 sales) is below US and Japanese peers.
tension_points.bear_case: The legislation could close gaps between US and allied regimes and extend restrictions around identified equipment and facilities, and the original text names some Chinese companies as warranting comprehensive export controls. A severe restriction on China immersion shipments with no tool reallocation would cut EPS by about 5-10% in 2027E/2028E.
tension_points.what_invalidates: China immersion shipments becoming largely restricted without reallocation of the affected tools to other customers, which is the UBS stress-test case.

theme_stances.key_argument: The MATCH Act does not create a blanket China DUV ban, and ASML's China exposure is now below US and Japanese peers.
theme_stances.evidence: MATCH does not simply say that all immersion DUV
